Many people will ask: since we already have full-text search, vector retrieval, and RAG, why do we still need GitNexus? The key is that code is not ordinary text. Code has clear structure, call relationships, dependency boundaries, and execution paths. Simply chopping code into fragments and searching can easily miss content that "does not appear in the same text block but is logically strongly related." A simple way to understand it is the following difference: Capability | Ordinary Search | General RAG | GitNexus
---|---|---|---
Search keywords | Yes | Yes | Yes
Find related code fragments | Weak | Yes | Yes
Understand call chains | Needs manual judgment | Unstable | More suitable
Analyze impact scope | Basically relies on experience | Depends on context | Can be queried via tools
Serve AI Agents | Indirect | Yes | Natively agent-oriented
The core idea of GitNexus can be summarized in one word: **precomputed relational intelligence**. That is, during the indexing phase, code structure, dependency relationships, call chains, functional clustering, and execution flows are all calculated. When an Agent actually executes a task, it does not get a pile of scattered fragments, but a project context that has been structurally organized.

8aaqxt:367: AI coding tools have evolved to the point where they are not just autocompleting a few lines of code. Tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex are gradually becoming true "partners" that can participate in the development process. But in real projects, one issue becomes increasingly obvious: ** AI isn't incapable of writing code—it's often unable to see the whole codebase. ** It may understand the current file, yet not know where else a function is called; it may complete a refactoring, but miss a cross-module dependency; sometimes it only changes an inconspicuous return value, and ends up affecting the entire downstream business flow. GitNexus aims to solve exactly this problem. It first organizes the codebase into a "knowledge graph," precomputing dependency relationships, call chains, functional clustering, and execution flows, then exposes them to AI Agents through MCP, CLI, Web UI, and more. In other words, GitNexus doesn't make the model "better at guessing"—it enables the model to truly understand your codebase before it starts changing code.
